question: With AsyncStorageWrites, do real MsgStorageAppendResp messages delayed across a real RawNode election leave unstable state unchanged when stale, and does a subsequently produced current-term response allow stabilization and application to resume? rationale: The accepted overview identifies term-qualified local completion as an A6 mechanism supporting A2 context validity and A1 application eligibility. Source guards already explain why blindly consuming old completions would be inappropriate; this exploration determines obtainable scheduling and producer observations before defining a formal Fact/requirement/check. Three RawNodes start from an explicitly constructed consistent snapshot prefix (index/term 1, voters 1/2/3) and use actual campaigns, proposals, replication, Ready production and Step delivery thereafter. MemoryStorage models completed ordered writes without crashes. Only node 3 local append-completion responses are finitely delayed, and they are ultimately delivered in production order; network acknowledgements remain eligible only after the corresponding modeled write. There are no protocol state assignments or fabricated response messages. The history has no suffix replacement, snapshot installation after initialization, configuration change or actual disk crash. A finite pump bound is a tool bound, not a liveness oracle.

feedback.answered: The source exposes an executable RawNode boundary for independently delaying local storage responses while continuing elections and replication.
